article.headline: Fastenal Holds Near Its 52-Week High On 20.7% Earnings Growth
article.deck: The fastener distributor sits 4.8% above its 53.02 buy point from a 12-week flat base, just under the top of the buy range at 55.67.
body: Fastenal traded at 55.55, up 6 cents or 0.1%, as of 1:48 p.m. Mountain. The stock broke out Nov. 4 from a 12-week flat base that corrected 10.6% from its Aug. 11 high to its Oct. 14 low. The buy point is 53.02 and the buy range runs to 55.67, so the stock is 4.8% past the buy point and 12 cents from the top of the range. The breakout session traded 1.48x the 50-day average volume; today is on pace for 0.35x.

Six sessions after the breakout, the stock sits 1.3% under its 52-week high of 56.27. It trades 8.6% above its 50-day line at 51.15 and above its 21-day line at 52.98, 1.9 ATRs from the 21-day line, a trend that is intact rather than stretched. The relative strength line is at a new high, and the stock ranks 79 of 99 on the desk's list. Fastenal is up 38.4% this year and 34.6% over 12 months.

In the September quarter, earnings rose 20.7% to 35 cents a share on revenue of $2.46 billion, up 15.5%. Earnings per share have climbed each quarter across the four in the table: 26 cents, 30 cents, 33 cents, 35 cents. The company is valued at about $63.7 billion at 39.3 times forward earnings. The next report is due Jan. 19, 2027.

The recent coverage is about the stock's run, not a new business event. A 24/7 Wall St. headline noted the shares are up 35% in 2026 and asked whether the dividend is still worth owning, and peer W.W. Grainger drew a headline for its best revenue growth in five years.
A close above 55.67 puts the stock out of the buy range.
article.watch: Whether it closes above the 55.67 top of the buy range or pulls back toward the 21-day line at 52.98.

article.headline: Microsoft Expands AI Ties With Ohio State; Shares Edge Higher
article.deck: A stalled breakout: the stock is 5.7% under its 553.82 buy point from a 51-week deep cup and is holding its 50-day line.
body: Microsoft traded at 522.22, up 1.09 or 0.2%, as of 1:48 p.m. Mountain. The stock broke out Nov. 4 past a 553.82 buy point from a 51-week deep cup that corrected 36.9%, with a buy range to 581.51, and that session traded 2.3x its 50-day average volume. Six sessions later it sits 5.7% under the buy point, a stalled breakout. Today is on pace for 0.59x average volume.

The pullback found the 50-day line. Microsoft trades 0.7% above that line at 518.71 and 1.2% below its 21-day line at 528.45, a reading of 0.0 ATRs from the 21-day line. The stock is 6.6% off its 52-week high of 559.15. The relative strength line is 9.6% under its high, and the stock ranks 64 of 99 on the desk's list. Shares are up 8.0% this year and 2.7% over 12 months.

In the September quarter, earnings rose 32.3% to $4.92 a share on revenue of $92.28 billion, up 18.8%. Quarterly revenue rose in each of the four quarters in the table, from $81.27 billion to $92.28 billion. The company is valued at about $3.88 trillion at 21.6 times forward earnings. The next report is due Jan. 27, 2027.

A Simply Wall St. headline said Microsoft expanded its AI ties with Ohio State. A 24/7 Wall St. headline grouped Microsoft with Alphabet and Amazon as gainers while Nvidia's leadership shake-up put Google's AI chips in the spotlight; Yahoo Finance ran a segment on what comes next for Nvidia after Jensen Huang's exit.
A close under the 50-day line would undo the bounce; a move back above 553.82 would put the breakout back in play.
article.watch: The 50-day line at 518.71 below and the 553.82 buy point above.

article.headline: Amgen Holds Steady After Sjogren's Drug Hits In Phase 3 Trial
article.deck: The biotech sits 4.7% above its 447.13 buy point from an eight-week cup, near the top of a buy range that ends at 469.49.
body: Amgen traded at 468.02, down 8 cents and flat in percentage terms, as of 1:48 p.m. Mountain. The stock broke out Oct. 22 from an eight-week cup that corrected 16.2% from its Aug. 25 high to its Sept. 16 low. The buy point is 447.13 and the buy range runs to 469.49; at 4.7% past the buy point the stock is 1.47 below the top of the range. The breakout session traded 1.11x the 50-day average volume, and today is on pace for 0.26x.

Fifteen sessions after the breakout, Amgen is 3.3% under its 52-week high of 483.99. It trades 10.2% above its 50-day line at 424.89 and above its 21-day line at 453.09, 1.18 ATRs from the 21-day line, so the trend is intact rather than stretched. The relative strength line is 1.5% off its high, and the stock ranks 90 of 99 on the desk's list. Shares are up 43.0% this year and 38.3% over 12 months.

In the September quarter, earnings rose 19.4% to $7.08 a share on revenue of $10.37 billion, up 8.5%. Earnings per share rose in each quarter across the table, from $2.45 to $3.34, $4.37 and $7.08. The company is valued at about $253.1 billion at 18.7 times forward earnings. The next report is due Feb. 2, 2027.

The news is the drug pipeline. Clinical Trials Arena reported that Amgen's acquired Sjogren's disease drug was a Phase 3 hit, and Investor's Business Daily headlined the data as rivaling Novartis. A GuruFocus headline counted 45 ETFs adding to their Amgen holdings on Tuesday.
A close above 469.49 takes the stock out of the buy range.
article.watch: The 469.49 top of the buy range and the 52-week high at 483.99.
